_comment: Computation-depth ladder. ONE argument set, four templates that differ only
in how much work stands between the swapped argument and the graded answer.
WHY. Across two evals the gsm8k-averaged lens gains most on first_letter and
least on retrieval templates, and the target-argument rank data says why:
at alpha=1.0 it drops median target_rank from 34 to 12 while the published
lens does not move it, and the templates whose rank improves are exactly the
templates whose steering improves. That says the corpus buys a cleaner
REBINDING, and that downstream computation attenuates the visible effect.
That reading is post-hoc. This eval tests it prospectively.
PREDICTION, recorded before running: the gsm8k gain over the published lens
decreases monotonically with depth -- largest at echo, smallest at family.
Holding the argument set fixed across all four rungs is the point: any
difference between rungs is the downstream operation alone, with the
arguments, the corpus and the intervention identical.
